title: MCP Conformance Engineering: Versioning, Evidence, and Operations
service: conformance: an MCP conformance harness with a release gate over redacted evidence, health and authenticated rollback pins, a one-file-per-case transcript fixture directory, response conformance rules for the 2026-07-28 and legacy eras, a proxy evidence stitcher that reports TAP, and an SDK differential over nested results
deviations: Part 1: the suggested timing case was 2,000 transcripts. The planted step redacts the whole corpus once per case, so 2,000 cases would take about a minute; the test uses 320 cases (about 1.5 s quadratic and 7 ms fixed on this machine, limit 0.15 s). The suggested defect 3 has two separate lines (a status blocklist that only refuses deleted, and pins checked for truthiness), so Part 1 has five layer steps for four defects. Health thresholds live in a HealthPolicy given to the gate, because the lesson says to define the health window before rollout; the lesson code reads them from the health dict itself.

Part 2: the fixture file holds the six suggested keys plus capabilities (Part 3 needs the negotiated Tasks capability) and expect (what a negative case proves). The file name is a lowercase slug, so names that differ only in case collide on every file system. Volatile values are taskId, createdAt and lastUpdatedAt, replaced by fixed values only when they are non-empty strings, so the malformed values of negative fixtures survive; JSON-RPC ids are chosen by the harness and are not normalized.

Part 3: response id checks are left out, as the chapter assigns JSON-RPC id types to lessons 06, 08 and 09. The lesson code reports every response violation as -32600, which cannot tell rules apart, so violations carry the harness's own rule names (wire.RULES) and a fixture's expect is either the server's error code or a rule name. 'input_required only for allowed methods' is tools/list and completion/complete answering only complete, as in the lesson code's validate_method_result; 'task only for tools/call' is tested with server/discover, because tools/list is already complete-only.

Part 4: time comes from the events' capture times (the clock is the largest at seen), and a deadline is timeout_ms after an exchange's first event, so the test is deterministic. 'Redact before judging' is read as: collectors at different boundaries ship in different redaction states, so the views are compared after redact(); an egress collector that redacts is not a body change. The ingress view is required evidence but is not judged, since request-side checks belong to lessons 06 and 09.

Part 5: a lift is a dropped member and a synthesized member with the same name and equal value, the synthesized one in an ancestor object; the allowance is keyed by the object's JSON Pointer and covers dropping only, so a synthesized or changed resultType is reported. Paths are RFC 6901 JSON Pointers.

Facts used beyond docs/en.md: the Registry statuses active, deprecated and deleted (lesson 30's docs); the task status set, the SECRET_KEYS list and the HTTP status map with -32021 to 400 and -32601 to 404 (this lesson's code/main.py). The rule names, the volatile placeholders and the TAP problem strings are this harness's own choices, stated in its docstrings.

parts.lesson_anchor: Redact Before Evidence Leaves Memory (canonical key names, recursive replacement, hash the redacted bundle); Make Health and Rollback Part of the Gate (minimum sample count, exact types, active status, three SHA-256 pins, trusted HMAC attestation; hold without a usable rollback target); code/main.py redact, evaluate_health, rollback_evidence_ready and ReleaseGate.evaluate
planted_bugs: redact looks the raw key up in SECRET_KEYS, which holds canonical forms, so Authorization, X-Api-Key, access_token, client.secret and Set-Cookie leak; the failure shows on the gate's report, two calls above redact (evaluate -> _transcripts -> redact), and canonical_field_name is written but unused

evaluate_health falls back to passing values: a missing sampleCount counts as min_samples, a missing errorRate or p95Ms as 0, so a canary with no samples promotes; failing defaults alone still raise TypeError on '1200'
rollback_evidence_ready refuses only registryStatus 'deleted', so 'deprecated', 'Active' and a missing status pass
rollback_evidence_ready checks the three pins for a non-empty string, so 'sha256:<hex>', 'pending' and 64 z's count as digests
evaluate computes each case digest from self._transcripts(cases), redacting the whole corpus once per case, O(n^2)
parts.timing_assert: 320 cases through ReleaseGate.evaluate under 0.15 s. Measured on this machine over several rounds: the quadratic version takes about 1.5 s (up to 4.9 s while other jobs pushed the load average to 50), the fixed version about 7 ms (median 14 ms and worst run 45 ms under that load); margins about 10x and 21x at the stable values
parts.overfix_guard: digests cover redacted evidence: rotating a bearer token leaves caseDigests and evidenceDigest unchanged, changing a stock count changes that case's digest and the bundle digest but not another case's, and a case digest equals digest(redact(evidence)); raw-evidence digests, a per-name digest cache, name-only digests, whole-record digests and one corpus digest for every case are all caught; checks that come with the fixes: a secret key's whole value is replaced even when it is an object or a list, and a float sampleCount fails the window

parts.lesson_anchor: Build a Transcript Corpus (fixture JSON with name, era, headers, request, responseStatus, responseBody; golden and negative classes; normalize volatile ids and timestamps); Record the selected era beside every transcript; Store fixture schemas in version control
parts.exactness: seven fixtures read back equal through a second corpus instance: header names with their case (Mcp-Method and mcp-method kept apart), a legacy era, a notification with no body (None, not {}), a non-ASCII name and arguments, a CRLF in the response text, frozenset capabilities through a sorted list, an int expect and a rule-name expect; the file holds exactly the documented record; re-recording a task call with other ids and timestamps writes byte-identical files

file name keeps case, keeps dots, replaces single characters, is not trimmed, or uses \W+ and keeps non-ASCII letters
a name with no letters or digits gets '.json'
no collision check, a collision judged by file name or without case, or noticed after the file was overwritten
an existing fixture never replaced
load trusts the file name; names() read from file names
a missing era read as modern or raising KeyError; a protocol version accepted as an era; the era not checked on save
capabilities as a list, in set order, or written with default=str; no body stored as {}; expect stored as text
fixtures cached in memory; an index file beside the fixtures
volatile values kept, not normalized inside lists or in the request, empty strings and non-strings replaced, or normalized in place

parts.lesson_anchor: Unknown Fields Are Not Unknown Results (additive futureHint accepted, unknown or unadvertised resultType rejected, task only with the Tasks capability for tools/call, method payloads for tools/list and completion/complete); Start With Version Eras (missing resultType is complete only in the selected legacy era); Negative transcripts (jsonrpc, result/error exclusivity, error shape, protocol errors on the wrong HTTP status, assert the exact rejection); The Notification Invariant (202 and no body, middleware wrapping None)
traps: unknown members rejected, or an unknown resultType read as complete; a dict resultType raising TypeError
payload checked before the discriminator

a missing resultType complete in every era, or required in legacy too; the method check reading the raw resultType; an inferred result skipping the payload or written back into the wire result; legacy accepting any resultType
input_required on complete-only methods; task as a core type, on any method, or looked up by a short capability name
tools/list: duplicate or empty names, non-object inputSchema, missing or empty description, missing schema, a missing tools array read as empty, tools assumed to be objects

completion: exactly 100 values rejected or 101 allowed, total checked for type only, coerced, a boolean, or required to exceed the values, string hasMore, unchecked items, missing values read as empty

error status unchecked, -32021 left out, -32601 mapped to 400, or every error forced into 4xx; result status unchecked; a None result read as {}; a request with no body accepted, or an empty object read as no body

check_case: any violation passes a negative, any error code passes a refusal, the expected code read from the body on HTTP 500, a golden case accepting a refusal, an accepted negative passing, snake_case evidence keys
parts.integration: fixtures saved through Part 2, checked with run_corpus and handed to the Part 1 gate: the conformant corpus promotes, and one fixture that misses its expectation rolls back with exactly that reason
clarifying_questions: HTTP status for other error codes

parts.lesson_anchor: Capture Proxy Evidence (ingress, origin and egress views; an origin 400 or 404 JSON-RPC error becoming a proxy 500; the egress body differing from the origin body); Redact Before Evidence Leaves Memory; code/main.py inspect_proxy
parts.wire_format: TAP: one 'ok N - id' or 'not ok N - id # problems' line per exchange, problems joined by '; ' in a fixed order, the plan '1..N' last, every line ending with a newline; decided by the test's regex and exact line list
traps: no plan line for an empty stream; lines without a newline
an exchange opened only by its ingress
views compared as captured, so a redacting collector looks like a body change
a collapse also reported as a status change; only 400 collapsible; any 400 or 404 body counted as a protocol error; other status changes ignored
problems in another order or joined with a comma
events counted instead of distinct views; a later copy of a view replacing the first; a reported exchange reopened by a late copy

overdue exchanges reported only at the end, by name, or expired before the event is applied; the deadline restarting with each view; the deadline itself counted as overdue; the clock taken from the latest event instead of the largest capture time
open exchanges at the end left out or sorted by name; missing views listed alphabetically
lines held until the stream ends (probe: events pulled when each line comes out)
clarifying_questions: a view after the exchange was reported
order of exchanges that time out together

parts.lesson_anchor: Add an SDK Differential (raw status and body versus the SDK-normalized value; fields lifted, synthesized, stripped or changed; SDK-only removal of resultType, _meta, ttlMs and cacheScope; a dropped futureHint is reported); Interactive Lab C and D
traps: bookkeeping dropped at any depth, or only the root entry of allowed honoured
bookkeeping the SDK adds or changes not reported
names not escaped, or escaped in the wrong order
lists compared by value, tail drops or extra SDK items ignored
values compared as text or with Python equality (true == 1); a list compared with an object item by item; a null member read as a missing one
raw members before the SDK's; differences sorted by path text

no lifts; a lift ignoring the value, reported at its destination, limited to one object up, allowed sideways or to any shallower object, or one synthesized member paired with every drop; pairing in a single pass, so a destination reported first is counted twice
parts.integration: differential_report feeds the Part 1 gate: the SDK view that drops futureHint rolls back, the one that keeps it promotes
